status: RESOLVED -- decision frozen by the project_lead
summary: The author repository contains two DCSI routines. The two-class routine matches the published Definition 3.2 and produced the published values we were able to recompute. The multiclass real-world routine doubles every separation entry through a symmetrisation step. Our primary comparator follows the definition; a diagnostic variant reproduces the multiclass routine so the difference stays auditable.

paper.plain: separation is THE MINIMUM distance between core points of the two classes

calc_DCSI.scope: two-class; used by the synthetic experiments and by the per-dataset measure table
calc_DCSI.separation: min over clusters of the minimum distance from that cluster's core points to core points outside it
calc_DCSI.returns: DCSI, Sep_DCSI, Conn_DCSI -- the exact names stored in the shipped result tables

calc_DCSI_RW.scope: multiclass real-world; returns a pairwise matrix
what_happens: the inner loop runs `for(j in 1:K) if(i != j)`, so it assigns BOTH Sep_matrix[i,j] AND Sep_matrix[j,i] with the same min distance
because both triangles were already populated, this doubles every separation entry
calc_DCSI_RW.effective_formula: Sep_effective = 2 * min distance between core points
calc_DCSI_RW.contrast_within_the_same_function: the pairwise dcsi_matrix immediately below uses `for(j in i:K)` (upper triangle only), so ITS `+ t()` symmetrisation is correct. Only Sep is doubled.

reference_implementation.characterisation: a localised symmetrisation slip in one of the two routines, not a disagreement about the mathematics: the definition, the two-class routine and the published values all agree with each other

component_level_evidence.level: core points, connectedness, separation, pairwise index and aggregate compared separately, because a matching total can hide two compensating component errors
component_level_evidence.validity_agreement: every input we declare undefined is also undefined for the reference

publication_value_reproduction.question: which mode do the authors' own published numbers correspond to?
publication_value_reproduction.method: the repository stores each synthetic experiment's raw data together with its computed measure table, so a published value can be recomputed end to end
publication_value_reproduction.also_reproduced: the published Sep_DCSI and Conn_DCSI components, not only the index
publication_value_reproduction.scope_limit: two synthetic K=2 cases were recomputable end to end; the real-world multiclass tables were not reproduced, so no claim is made about which routine produced those
publication_value_reproduction.correction_to_earlier_note: an earlier version of this file assumed the published numbers had been produced by calc_DCSI_RW and therefore corresponded to the doubled variant. That assumption was wrong: the checkable published values reproduce exactly under the paper-faithful definition.

ranking_equivalence.earlier_claim: rankings are unaffected, therefore no conclusion depends on the choice
ranking_equivalence.status: WITHDRAWN -- the claim is false in general
ranking_equivalence.what_is_actually_true: the pairwise score is strictly increasing in q under both modes, so for K=2 the two modes order candidates identically
ranking_equivalence.what_is_false: for K>=3 the multiclass value is the MEAN of a nonlinear transform, and mean(q/(1+q)) and mean(2q/(1+2q)) can order two candidates differently
ranking_equivalence.empirical_counterexample: also produced through the shipped implementation on random K=3 configurations, so the reversal is not an artifact of hand-chosen q values

primary_comparator.definition: Sep = min distance between core points (Definition 3.2)
primary_comparator.role: one of exactly four modern comparators (CDbw, CVNN, CVDD, DCSI)
primary_comparator.justification: it is what the paper defines and what the authors' own published values reproduce

diagnostic_variant.definition: Sep = 2 x the above, reproducing calc_DCSI_RW
diagnostic_variant.role: AUTHOR-IMPLEMENTATION-COMPATIBILITY diagnostic and predeclared sensitivity variant

frozen_decision.implementation: ONE shared implementation with an explicit frozen `sep_mode` switch, so the exact difference is a single auditable line rather than a duplicated code path

wording_guidance: Describe this as a localised implementation discrepancy between one routine and the published definition, evidenced at component level and by reproduction of the authors' own published values. Do not characterise the metric or the authors' work as wrong: the definition is unambiguous, the two-class routine implements it correctly, and the published values we could check are paper-faithful.
